# EStyle / elk-style-rule

EStyle is a framework-independent, type-safe CSS-in-JS package for TypeScript.
The npm package name is `elk-style-rule`. The main export is the `Estyle` class.
Source repository: https://github.com/ElktrumElk/EStyle
Primary examples and concepts: https://github.com/ElktrumElk/EStyle/blob/main/docs/README.md
Focused usage guide: https://github.com/ElktrumElk/EStyle/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md

## Install

`npm install elk-style-rule`

## Import

`import { Estyle } from "elk-style-rule";`

## Primary workflow

1. Create `new Estyle({ namespace?, autoInject?, prepend?, nonce?, strategy? })`.
2. Call `.defineRules({ ruleName: { ...typedCss } })`.
3. Put pseudo classes, pseudo elements, attribute, compound, and descendant
   selectors in nested keys that begin with `&`, for example `"&:hover"`,
   `"&::before"`, or `"& .icon"`.
4. Optionally call `.defineKeyframes({ name: { from: {...}, to: {...} } })` and
   reference `styles.keyframes.name` as an `animationName`.
5. Optionally call `.defineMedia({ "(max-width: 600px)": { ruleName: {...} } })`.
6. Call `.mount("stable-namespace")` to choose the namespace and ensure the
   stylesheet is attached.
7. Apply `styles.classes.ruleName` as a class or use
   `styles.rule.ruleName(overrides)` as an inline style object.
8. Call `.destroy()` for dynamically-created sheets.

## Why mount exists

`defineRules` stores typed JavaScript definitions. Browsers cannot apply a class
name until corresponding CSS exists. EStyle serializes base rules, pseudo
classes and elements, nested selectors, `@keyframes`, and `defineMedia` rules
into one managed stylesheet. By default (`autoInject: true`) this stylesheet is
injected synchronously as rules are defined and inserted at the front of `<head>`
so the page never flashes an unstyled state. `mount(namespace)` selects the
deterministic namespace used for classes, keyframes, and the sheet. `classes` and
`className` are available without mounting, but mounting fixes the namespace.
Use `styles.getStyles()` for server-rendered critical CSS. Use the selector-free
`rule` inline-style accessor when no generated CSS is needed.

## Capabilities

- Typed CSS properties through `csstype`
- Stable generated class names
- Hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, and arbitrary safe nested selectors
- Pseudo elements such as `::before`, `::after`, and `::placeholder`
- Typed `@keyframes` with collision-free generated animation names
- Attribute and descendant selectors
- Declarative CSS media queries
- Typed light and dark theme token records
- CSS custom properties
- Instant, synchronous style injection (no flash of unstyled content)
- Critical CSS extraction with `getStyles()` for server rendering
- Style element, adopted stylesheet, and matchMedia listener cleanup
- No React or other UI framework runtime dependency

## Minimal example

```ts
const styles = new Estyle();

styles.defineKeyframes({
  fadeIn: { from: { opacity: 0 }, to: { opacity: 1 } },
});

styles
  .defineRules({
    button: {
      color: "white",
      backgroundColor: "#173f36",
      animationName: styles.keyframes.fadeIn,
      "&:hover": { backgroundColor: "#d75632" },
      "&::before": { content: "\"→\"" },
    },
  })
  .mount("controls");

element.className = styles.classes.button;
```

Use `defineMedia` instead of imperative `mediaQuery` for normal responsive CSS.
Use the `rule` accessor only when an inline style object is needed; nested
selectors and pseudo elements are omitted from inline output. Use `getStyles()`
to inline critical CSS during server rendering.
